title: RevLens — MRR Forecasting & Reproducible Revenue Analytics
role: Data Scientist & Data Engineer / Full-Stack Developer
summary: I built a local pipeline that turns subscription CSVs into reconciled MRR, an evaluated 1–3 month forecast and exportable evidence. Python compares statistical methods against a last-value baseline using temporal validation. SQL/dbt marts, PostgreSQL SCD2 and revision-bound checkpoints keep results traceable and recovery safe. The public demo uses fictional MRR; a separate real retail benchmark does not establish SaaS accuracy.
problem: Revenue dashboards often mix descriptive metrics, manual scenarios and predictions without showing which is which. Imported corrections also need traceable history and a recoverable analytical pipeline.
solution: RevLens separates statistical forecasts from what-if planning. Dated subscription facts feed tested dbt views; native snapshots capture customer and plan changes. Python compares three transparent methods, evaluates them without using future observations, and exposes the evidence in the UI.
pipeline: Validated CSV → transactional raw save and revision → dbt snapshots, views and tests → temporal model evaluation → 1–3 month prediction → tables and JSON export.
recovery: Before restoring or changing source, the local server fsyncs an automatic checkpoint of raw records, source metadata and native SCD2 outside the repository. Revision checks prevent concurrent overwrites. Discarding an uncaptured revision requires its own confirmation. Failed writes abort replacement; failed analytics preserve records, hide stale versions and allow retry. Checkpoints exclude accounts and credentials and are retained until manually archived.
limits: Personal portfolio project. Synthetic subscriptions do not establish real SaaS accuracy or business impact. The real benchmark measures GBP retail sales, not MRR. Local, single-operator and USD-only imports; no individual churn prediction, causal claims, cloud scheduler or live CRM delivery.

delivery.label: Input
delivery.text: USD subscription history in CSV. An evaluated forecast requires at least 24 confirmed complete months; no unknown months are fabricated.

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.text: Reconciled MRR, 1–3 month forecasts, last-value baseline, errors by horizon, nominal intervals, tables/JSON and reproducible instructions.

delivery.label: Short history
delivery.text: Coverage diagnosis and descriptive analytics remain available. No evaluated forecast is shown until the history requirement is met.

delivery.label: Scope
delivery.text: Personal project with fictional SaaS MRR and a separate real retail benchmark. No demonstrated real-SaaS accuracy, financial impact or promised accuracy for a buyer.

readmeInstructions:
## Run the static demo

Requires Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm 10.32.1, with no database or API key:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Wild-Badger/revlens.git
cd revlens
corepack enable
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm demo:build
pnpm demo:preview
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:3102/revlens/. The adapter reuses application screens and fictional exports. Hash routes support reloads; scenario arithmetic remains interactive.

## Run your private workspace

Windows prerequisites: Node.js, pnpm, **PostgreSQL 17** and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/). uv resolves Python 3.12 and installs the locked environment.

```powershell
.\scripts\start-local.ps1 -Mode Check
.\scripts\start-local.ps1
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:3101/signup once to create the owner. The launcher starts a dedicated initially empty PostgreSQL cluster on port 55433, Python on **127.0.0.1:8101** and Next.js on **127.0.0.1:3101**. Private credentials, logs, environment and database live outside the repository in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RevLensLocalWorkspace`. Existing owner credentials remain valid; no sample customers are seeded. `-SkipBuild` reuses a build; rebuild after code changes. Ctrl+C stops Next.js and its Python child; PostgreSQL stays running.

In **Import data**, identify an update to the current source or replacement by a new source, supply the observation date, first complete month and coverage confirmation. Unknown history stays unknown. New sources require a revision-bound confirmation. An automatic durable checkpoint saves the prior source before its active captured history is reset. Download and archive checkpoints from Data workspace. Stable `subscription_id` values identify constant-MRR intervals; adjacent intervals support price changes and reactivation. Overlapping intervals per customer are rejected. Optional `plan_id`, `plan_base_price`, `plan_seat_price` preserve catalog facts; absent prices stay null.

Limits: 2 MiB CSV, 2,000 rows, 10,000 product events and 25 MiB backups. Backup v2 includes source metadata and native snapshots. v1 restores with prior coverage/history unknown. Authentication is preserved but does not encrypt files on disk; keep loopback private.

Restore also requires the displayed dataset revision; pending changes need explicit revision-specific discard confirmation. An unwritable checkpoint aborts before deletion. Checkpoints use a versioned checksum envelope; downloading is owner-only and restoring applies normal validation. Raw invalid revisions remain downloadable for manual recovery. Checkpoints are retained outside the repository and are never automatically deleted.

After raw save, dbt captures snapshots, builds views and tests. Failure shows **data saved, analytics pending**, blocks ordinary same-source updates and permits retry. Restore can replace a pending revision only after its explicit discard confirmation. Old marts cannot appear current. SCD2 starts with observed captures, never invented historical versions.

## Verify

```sh
uv sync --frozen --all-groups --python 3.12
pnpm exec prisma generate
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm test --maxWorkers=2
uv run python -m pytest -q
pnpm lint
pnpm demo:build
```

[Database reproduction and release checks](docs/verification.md) use dedicated loopback databases ending in `_demo` or `_test`. Seed/export scripts reject unrelated populated databases. CI provisions temporary PostgreSQL, exercises import/SCD2/backup recovery, regenerates artifacts and builds both applications before Pages deployment.

## Structure and scope

- `analytics/`: Python engine, local API, fixtures and benchmark reports.
- `dbt/`: tested analytical views and persistent native SCD2.
- `app/`, `lib/`: Next.js, authenticated APIs, Prisma and warehouse readers.
- `demo/`: shared-screen static adapter and fictional export.
- `scripts/`, `docs/`: launcher, verification, presentation generator and evidence.

Runtime analytical reads use dbt marts; customer/invoice operations use Prisma. Retained TypeScript calculations are unit-test regression oracles. Legacy `/api/analytics/forecast` returns 410 with its replacement. CRM/billing adapter source is outside the verified workflow and its webhooks are disabled in local mode. No queue worker, Redis alerts, managed warehouse or always-on cloud service is claimed.

## Hosting

GitHub Pages needs **no daily renewal, paid API or hosting subscription**. Private training and imports run on your computer. [Official documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages) and [usage limits](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/github-pages-limits) apply. Upwork materials stay local pending separate approval.
